title: Redwood cost/econ discovery with Stratus Ventures
next_steps: Send tailored pricing sheet and cost model by 2026-03-06
Share dedicated capacity SLA doc and KMS whitepaper
Schedule a 60-min POC scoping call w/ infra on 2026-03-10
action_items: Maya: Share perf benchmark template + sample KV cache config (due 2026-03-06)
Lena: Provide sample traffic profile and current token volumes (due 2026-03-08)
summary: Customer is evaluating Redwood for inference across hosted vs dedicated vs private for a recommendation engine and internal analyst tools.
Primary focus: per-token unit economics, batching/caching levers, and budget constraints for Q2 pilot.
Customer leans toward Dedicated if cost/throughput tradeoffs and security (VPC/KMS) are acceptable.
Next: pricing sheet, SLA/KMS docs, POC scoping call to define benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Tom (Stratus - CTO): Tom here.
[00:06] Lena (Head of ML Ops): Lena.
[00:08] Samir (Finance): Samir.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood SE): Maya from Redwood, hi.
[00:15] Ethan: Cool, high level agenda — cost/unit economics, what you run today, constraints, and then we can go into hosting modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and levers like batching, cache, quantization. Anything to add?
[00:25] Tom: No that's it. We're under time pressure, want quick numbers to present to execs next week.
[00:30] Ethan: Great. Can you give us a rough of current usage and budget?
[00:40] Lena: Sure. Right now inference is on BigCloud AI managed endpoints for our recommendation scoring. About 80M tokens/day total, peaks around 6x. Latency SLOs are 150ms p95 for interactive internal analyst queries, but recommendation scoring can tolerate up to 500ms.
[00:55] Samir: Our raw budget for LLM ops next quarter is ~120k USD but that has to include storage and infra. So ideally inference below 60k/mo.
[01:05] Maya: Got it. For context, Redwood hosted pricing has per-token and optional reserved capacity discounts — our pricing model is per input/output token. We also have Dedicated which is reserved GPU pools that gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost per token when you're high volume.
[01:20] Tom: How much lower? ballpark numbers are fine.
[01:26] Ethan: Ballpark: on hosted at this scale, depending on model, you're in the mid-single-digit cents per 1k tokens for some larger gen models, but with batching and KV caching you can reduce effective cost 2-4x. For Dedicated reserved capacity we can get to roughly half or a third of hosted marginal rates, especially if you can tolerate some setup for batching and quantization. (note: numbers approximate)
[01:50] Lena: When you say batching and KV cache — how does that work with our interactive p95 requirement? can't add too much latency.
[01:58] Maya: Right. We do continuous batching on the runtime — it groups requests across a short window, like 5-20ms, and leverages prefix KV cache to serve cached tokens instantly for repeated contexts. For analyst queries with high tail sensitivity we suggest hybrid: low-latency tier routed to small dedicated nodes (or hosted with lower batching) and background scoring on cheaper batched nodes.
[02:20] Tom: So multi-tier routing. That makes sense. What's the tradeoff on the billing side? if we split tiers do we pay for each?
[02:28] Ethan: You pay for the workload executed. If the cached responses avoid recomputation, they don't consume compute tokens in the same way — they'll still count in some cases depending on payload, but overall you save on compute time. We can show a model: e.g., if KV cache hits 40% of tokens and batching improves throughput 3x, your effective per-token compute cost goes down proportionally.
[02:45] Samir: Ok can you share a sample calc? we need to show finance difference between hosted vs dedicated break-even.
[02:51] Maya: Yes — we'll put together a cost model. Quick rough: assume base hosted cost X per 1k tokens. With 40% cache hit and batching 3x you'd get effective cost ~0.2-0.3X. Dedicated reserved reduces per-hour GPU cost, so if you're consistently at high utilization you'll get further 2-3x reduction over hosted marginal rates.
[03:10] Tom: Are there minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[03:13] Ethan: Dedicated is reserved pools; typical contracts are monthly/annual reserved capacity. Minimums depend on configuration but most customers start with a modest commit to reserve a few GPUs and scale. We can be flexible for pilot.
[03:25] Lena: Is quantization supported? we run large 7B- model family and want 8-bit quant to save cost.
[03:30] Maya: Yes, our runtime supports quantization-friendly paths and optimized kernels. Quantization often reduces memory footprint and can increase throughput, but there are model-specific quality tradeoffs. We usually recommend running A/B evals on quality and serving fallback on critical routes.
[03:45] Tom: About security — we need VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2, and SSO. Is that all supported on Dedicated or Private?
[03:53] Ethan: Yes. Dedicated includes VPC/VPN options, KMS integration, RBAC, audit logs. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane for stricter requirements and on-prem options. Hosted can support some enterprise integrations but if you absolutely must have customer-managed keys and air-gapped, Private is the option.
[04:10] Samir: Any price delta for Private?
[04:12] Ethan: Private typically is enterprise license + deployment costs. It's less about per-token and more about upfront platform license and support. We can provide a TCO comparison.
[04:20] Lena: For our case, security is important but not airgap-level. KMS + VPC should suffice.
[04:24] Tom: Back to cost: what about burst pricing and autoscaling? We have spiky loads and don't want to pay for reserved GPUs we don't use.
[04:33] Maya: Dedicated can have configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity to hosted spare capacity. You pay for reserved baseline and then burst usage at a different marginal rate. The platform also supports policy-based routing to spill to hosted when Dedicated is at capacity.
[04:46] Tom: So hybrid is doable — reserved base + hosted overflow.
[04:49] Ethan: Exactly. Many customers do that to control costs while handling spikes.
[04:52] Samir: Let's talk numbers again: if our monthly token is 80M/day *30 = 2.4B tokens/month. Using rough hosted cost of 0.04 USD per 1k tokens (example), that would be 96k/mo, over our 60k target. So we need at least 2x reduction to fit.
[05:12] Maya: Right if that's the hosted baseline, caching and batching that we discussed can help. Also switching to Dedicated and quantized LLMs can yield additional savings. Also consider model selection: smaller open models with Redwood-verified perf may be cheaper per token.
[05:26] Tom: What's the work needed to benchmark — can we run a short POC to measure cache hit rates and batching gains?
[05:33] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC plan: share traffic profile and sample prompts, Redwood runs benchmarks on hosted and dedicated configs with quantization and batching knobs, returns a cost model and perf numbers. That usually takes 1-2 weeks.
[05:45] Lena: We'll need to know how you measure tokens — is it input+output or just output?
[05:49] Ethan: We bill on input + output tokens. We also provide token-level breakdown and per-route cost analytics in Console so you can see which routes are expensive.
[05:58] Tom: Is there any additional charge for KV cache storage?
[06:01] Maya: KV cache is part of the serving runtime — there may be small storage fees for very large persistent caches on Private, but generally it's included. We'll clarify in the docs.
[06:10] Samir: Another question: if we have sensitive PII in prompts, how does hosted handle that?
[06:15] Ethan: Hosted can be configured to not retain user prompts and to integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest; for stricter needs, Dedicated or Private keeps data isolated. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[06:25] Tom: competitors — why Redwood vs BigCloud AI or FastServe?
[06:28] Maya: Two big differentiators: production-first observability and cost controls. We surface token-level cost, batching knobs, and automatic KV caching recommendations; plus unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private so your dev experience is consistent.
[06:42] Tom: Alright, can you walk through a sample calc in the meeting?
[06:46] Ethan: Sure. Let's use your 2.4B tokens/month. Assume hosted baseline 0.04 per 1k tokens -> 96k/mo. If KV cache hits 40% and batching x3, model effective compute reduces. Simple way: compute-cost = baseline * (1 - cache_hit) / batching_factor -> 0.04 * (0.6) / 3 = 0.008 per 1k tokens effective. Multiply -> 19.2k/mo. That's before Dedicated reserved discounts. If dedicated gives 50% lower per compute unit, you'd be ~9.6k/mo. Obviously simplified, but shows the levers.
[07:25] Lena: That math helps. But real cache hits vary by route; recommendations might have high hit, analyst queries low.
[07:31] Maya: Exactly — per-route breakdown is key. Console provides per-route token counts and we can run evals to estimate cacheable prefix share.
[07:40] Tom: About billing granularity: can we set per-route budgets and alerts?
[07:45] Ethan: Yes. Console supports budgets, rate limits, and alerting per API key/route.
[07:50] Samir: For the POC, we want two scenarios: 1) conservative cache 20% 2) aggressive 50% — show cost outcomes. Also compare hosted-only vs dedicated baseline + burst.
[08:00] Maya: We can do that. We'll need sample traffic CSV and list of prompt templates to simulate cacheability.
[08:07] Lena: We'll provide. Also question on throughput: if we go Dedicated, what's the typical tokens/sec per GPU for our model family?
[08:15] Maya: It depends on model size and sequence length. For a quantized 7B on A100-class GPU with optimized kernels you might see tens of thousands tokens/sec for streaming decode in batched mode. For shorter sequences you'll get higher throughput. We'll include model-specific numbers in the benchmark.
[08:33] Tom: Any hidden fees? e.g., network egress between regions?
[08:37] Ethan: Network egress follows normal cloud provider pricing if using Private on-prem or cross-region routing; hosted includes region pricing but we'll call out egress in the TCO.
[08:46] Samir: Ok. Regarding legal — we will want the standard DPA and append SOC2 in the scoping.
[08:52] Ethan: Noted. We'll attach SOC2 and SSO/SAML guides.
[08:56] Tom: Timeline — can we prove out within 4 weeks? execs want a recommendation in 6 weeks.
[09:01] Maya: POC 2 weeks for benchmarks, 1 week to analyze and iterate, plus time to sign if needed. 4 weeks is feasible if we get prompt samples and traffic profile today.
[09:10] Lena: Tom and I will compile the traffic profile.
[09:14] Ethan: Great. Any other concerns?
[09:16] Speaker 1 (intern?): one quick — do you support function calling / structured outputs?
[09:21] Maya: Yes, streaming and structured outputs are supported; results can be post-processed or routed to tools.
[09:26] Tom: On the subject of model fallback — if quantized variant drifts we want automatic fallback to full-precision model. is that supported?
[09:33] Maya: Yes, the runtime supports model variant routing with automatic fallback policies on quality regressions or latencies. We can tie that into rollouts and A/B tests.
[09:41] Tom: Good. Let's recap next steps.
[09:44] Ethan: Recap: we'll send pricing + cost model, perf benchmark template, SLA/KMS/security docs. We'll scope a POC to run benchmarks for hosted and dedicated with 2 cache scenarios. POC scoping call scheduled. Any dates?
[09:56] Tom: 2026-03-10 works for the scoping call.
[09:59] Samir: We expect pricing deck before 2026-03-06.
[10:03] Ethan: Noted. I'll get that out.
[10:06] Lena: One last nit — how do you handle billing auditability? we need line-item per-route cost for our FinOps.
[10:12] Ethan: Console provides token-level cost breakdown by route and model; we'll export CSV for your FinOps.
[10:18] Tom: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[10:20] Ethan: Thanks — we'll follow up.
[10:24] [end of recording]
notes: POC focused on measuring KV cache hit rates and batching benefits; two scenarios requested (20% and 50% cache)
Customer target budget mismatch with naive hosted baseline; Dedicated + caching likely required to meet 60k/mo target
